newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia, U.S. NRG sign power deal.
newsitem.headline: Estonia, U.S. NRG sign power deal.

text.p: The Estonian goverment, power producer Estonian Energy and U.S. group NRG Energy, part of Northern States Power, on Friday signed a deal to create a joint-venture to operate Estonia's two biggest power plants.

"Our goal is to create a strong power company in cooperation with Estonian Energy effectively to produce electricity for the Estonian people as well as industry," David Peterson, NRG Energy chief, told a news conference.
He said the deal would also solve potential environmental, social and economic problems.
The joint project consists of a business plan and a techical and economic analysis of the two plants, both of which use oil shale and produce some 96 percent of Estonian electricity.
"This is a historic event in the Estonian power industry," said Economy Minister Jaak Leiman.
NRG Energy intends to invest about $250 million in the joint firm, the biggest foreign investment so far in Estonia.
"This is a long-term investment which should lead the energy plants to world-class standard," said Peterson.
He said the power may also be exported.

Arvi Hamburg, economy minister deputy chancellor, said the price for electricity would definetely rise but it would be a smaller increase than if the reconstruction of the plants took place using domestic funds.
He said that other possible investors would still have the chance to take part in the privatisation of the transmission and distribution network.
